preamble: The elision of [z] is a common stage of sound weakening, often following a debuccalization path. In the history of Korean, the Middle Korean voiced sibilant ㅿ /z/ disappeared between vowels, as in ᄆᆞᅀᆞᆷ mʌzʌm 'heart, mind' > 마음 maŭm.

examples.note: Middle Korean ㅿ /z/ (a lenition product of *s) disappeared by the 16th century; some southeastern dialects keep s

sources: Lee, K.-M., & Ramsey, S. R. (2011). A History of the Korean Language. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511974045
